subject: Request: On-Prem Latency Attribution Waiver & SLA Addendum
messages:
From: Alicia Mendes <alicia@quantumfold.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantumfold.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: On-Prem Latency Attribution Waiver & SLA Addendum

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this — we’re in the final stages of a private deployment with Redwood in our primary cluster and have run into a governance requirement from our platform team. Because QuantumFold is running the customer-side edge/NAT and we’re colocated with a regional transit provider, our security and ops teams need a written carveout in the SLA for any availability/latency incidents that can be attributed to customer-controlled edge devices or third-party transit outside Redwood’s backbone.

Specifically we’re asking for:
- A short addendum that excludes latency/uptime credits where monitoring and packet-level evidence show the root cause lies in our edge (customer-owned) devices or in third-party transit nodes beyond our ASN.
- A clear evidence checklist (packet captures, traceroutes, BGP announcements) the parties will accept for attribution.
- A one-time onboarding credit if attribution tooling is not available during cutover.

I’ve attached our architecture diagram and a short evidence packet showing a recent spike where the first hop after our NAT showed sustained RTT increase. Can your team propose addendum language and an evidence matrix so legal can review quickly? We’d like to land this before go‑live (targeting 12/10).

Best,
Alicia Mendes
Head of Platform Engineering
QuantumFold AI

Attachments: architecture_diagram.png (image), initial_evidence_packet.pdf (pdf)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Mendes <alicia@quantumfold.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Dec 2029 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: On-Prem Latency Attribution Waiver & SLA Addendum

Hi Alicia — thanks for the context and the attachments.

We can accommodate a narrowly scoped attribution carveout for customer-controlled edge/network elements, but to make this operational and defensible we need three things from your side:

1) A one-page evidence matrix describing what counts as conclusive attribution (pcap windows, traceroute/hops to highlight, timing correlation thresholds).
2) A short runbook that shows how QuantumFold will collect/retain telemetry for incidents (who has access, retention window, and tooling).
3) A signed scoping sheet that identifies the customer-owned ASN(s) and colo partner (so we can codify the boundary).

I’m attaching a draft SLA addendum template (sla_addendum_template_v0.1.docx) with suggested language we typically use for private deployments. Priyom — can you take a technical pass on the wording and the evidence checklist? Rishi — I’ve looped you for the commercial/credit ask so we can propose acceptable on‑boarding credit options. Naomi, please hold for compliance evidence retention questions.

Proposed next steps:
- Priyom returns edited addendum + checklist by EOD Monday 12/02
- QuantumFold provides final evidence matrix and ASN list by 12/04
- We push to Legal/Docs for a DocuSign route by 12/06 if all good

If that timeline works let me know and I’ll shepherd legal.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla_addendum_template_v0.1.docx

Hi team — quick technical assessment based on the diagram and the initial pcap:

Summary: The packet captures show the first sustained RTT inflation at the hop that appears to be the customer NAT (per your diagram). That pattern is consistent with customer-side queuing or a transit provider upstream.

What I’d propose we require to accept customer attribution:
- Time-synchronized pcap snippets on both sides (customer edge and Redwood ingress) with NTP-synced timestamps for a 60s window around the incident.
- Traceroute from the customer edge and from Redwood server to the customer endpoint taken within the same minute, showing consistent hop where delta jumps >30ms.
- BGP table snapshot demonstrating the customer’s announced ASN for the prefix in question.
- Optional: tcpdump evidence of queueing (retransmits, duplicated ACKs) if the customer can provide it.

Draft wording suggestion (short):
"Redwood Inference shall not be liable for availability or latency degradation that is conclusively shown to originate within Customer-controlled network devices, Customer-owned ASN advertising, or third-party network providers outside the network hops under Redwood’s operational control. Conclusive attribution requires the evidence set defined in Appendix A (time-synced pcaps, paired traceroutes, and/or BGP snapshot)."

Operational note: We should also specify a 14-day window for customers to produce evidence after incident notification; otherwise it defaults to Redwood investigation. If the customer cannot provide the evidence, the incident will be investigated by Redwood and looked at under the standard SLA process.

I’ve attached a short checklist (network_attribution_checklist.xlsx) to include as Appendix A. Happy to iterate.

—Priyom
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — important context. Commercial POV: we can accept the narrowly scoped carveout, provided we also:

1) Keep the language tight (Priyom’s Appendix A + time windows).
2) Exclude credits for incidents where attribution is customer-controlled.
3) Offer a limited onboarding concession: a one-time credit equivalent to 10% of the first 3 months’ hosted usage fees (applied as account credit) if QuantumFold is unable to produce the required evidence during the initial cutover period.

We should make the onboarding credit conditional (one-time, non-recurring) and tie it to acceptance of the SLA addendum via signature. Also request legal to confirm there aren’t broader indemnity exposures. If legal needs different phrasing we’ll incorporate.

Vanessa — if that’s acceptable I’ll ask Legal to draft the final credit language and Naomi can confirm retention/compliance questions.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
